behaviors.scope: Intentional bounded native throughput policy for finite guarded32 World: reusable R32UI scratch snapshots of only the blend/additive destination rectangle or displacement rectangle plus admitted rightward reach; original RGB565 arithmetic, absolute displacement row phase, strict known-pixel admission and draw ordering remain. V1/V2 and per-raster handshakes retain their existing immediate writes. Native consumer drains finite guarded batches without per256record timer gaps, with a bounded per-tick budget and unchanged checkpoint/CPU/GPU/original pixel comparisons. Tight RGB565 packing preserves wire bytes. Diagnostic correctness and warm consumer throughput on software Mesa are separate from full simulation cadence, continuous/hardware rendering and normal-mode gameplay. Consecutive opaque copy rectangles with identical source/mask/destination/key and indexed policy, carrying per-instance palette row from at most64owned256word palettes in a private256x64 R32UI bank are instanced in original order, at most512instances; source/destination mutations, blends, reads, storage deletion and outer batch exits flush pending copies. Full original checkpoint bytes are emitted in one write when original stride equals width; padded rows retain exact row writes. No shader blend arithmetic or original simulation changes. Per-raster JSON diagnostic objects are serialized after finite completion; compact ordered identity tuples remain bounded by the admitted stream and descriptor counts. Every descriptor still undergoes full source/AX/identity validation before publishing a reply. Closed producer-frame extent, header and normalized-pointer admission remain mandatory; the discarded per-draw identity hash is removed, while WorldIdentityCache retains exact owned bytes/tag identity and verifies resource revisions. Partially defined atlas pages retain at most512 proven write rectangles; only contained reads bypass the authoritative per-pixel validity scan, proof eviction falls back to that map, and invalidation clears every proof. V3 owned replay also uses the bounded4096-record drain budget. Source FNV and reply packing preserve canonical little-endian bytes/checksums while streaming into one owned completion buffer instead of copying temporary vectors. Closed owned replay skips live per-raster reply-file polling when DONE exists; marker and native proof validation remain mandatory, live guarded replies are unchanged. Warm median budgets on the declared software-Mesa host are50ms native work (CPU reference, adoption, preparation, GPU submission/readback/comparison) and100ms diagnostic queue wall time including transport, checkpoint artifacts and reply waits. These budgets do not assert50ms simulation frames; cold uploads, full-session cadence and continuous/hardware gameplay remain separate. On contexts advertising OpenGL4.3 or ARB_copy_image and its entry point, regional snapshots use same-format copy-image;3.3 framebuffer copy remains the fallback. Both paths preserve preceding writes and distinct scratch storage, checked against scalar pixels. Software-Mesa performance runs pin eight workers on the measured12-core host; public regression runner defaults to eight while preserving explicit caller thread settings. All before/after comparisons use the same worker count; hardware performance is not inferred.
